# July 2026 U.S. National Consumer Credit Trends Report


September 03, 2026


#### Highlights:


-


As of July 2026, total U.S. consumer debt reached $18.23 trillion, representing a 1.6% year-over-year increase, with mortgage debt maintaining a dominant 74% share of the total market.


-


Total non-mortgage debt reached $4.74 trillion, with auto loans and leases accounting for 36.5% and student loans making up 27.1% of the non-mortgage portfolio.


As of July 2026, the monthly Equifax[Consumer Credit Trends Report](https://www.equifax.com/resource/-/asset/report/monthly-national-consumer-credit-trends-report-june-2026-portfolio/) showed that total U.S. consumer debt was $18.23 trillion, up 1.6% from July 2025. Mortgage debt, including home equity loans, accounted for $13.49 trillion, a 74.0% share of total consumer debt, while non-mortgage consumer debt totaled $4.74 trillion, with 36.5% of non-mortgage consumer debt attributable to auto loans and leases, and 27.1% attributable to student loans.


Outstanding balances on auto loans and leases increased 3.3% from July 2025, to $1.73 trillion in July 2026.


Outstanding balances on U.S. bankcards increased versus the prior month to $1.14 trillion in July 2026, up 3.8% from July 2025. Average bankcard utilization stood at 20.4%, which is a slight decrease from 20.8% in July 2025.

#### Consumer Credit Observations:


-


As of July 2026, total U.S. consumer debt was $18.23 trillion, up 1.6% from July 2025.


-


Mortgage debt, including home equity loans, accounted for $13.49 trillion, making up 74.0% of total U.S. consumer debt.


-


First mortgages were 94.9% of mortgage debt outstanding.


-


Home Equity Lines of Credit (HELOCs) were 3.3% of mortgage debt outstanding.


-


Non-mortgage debt totaled $4.74 trillion in July 2026 and broke down into:


-


36.5% from auto loans and leases,


-


27.1% from student loans,


-


24.6% from credit card balances, and


-


11.8% from other products.


#### Auto Loans and Leases Observations:


-


Total outstanding balances on auto loans and leases increased 3.3% from July 2025 to $1.73 trillion.


-


The number of outstanding accounts in July 2026 was 87.9 million, a 1% increase year-over-year.


-


The severe balance delinquency (60+ days past due) rate in July 2026 was 1.46%, which is five basis points down from July of last year.


#### Bankcard Portfolio Observations:


-


Outstanding balances on bankcards increased 3.8% from July 2025 to $1.14 trillion.


-


The number of outstanding accounts was 599.7 million in July 2026, a 2.9% increase from July 2025.


-


The severe balance delinquency rate (60+ days past due) as of July 2026 was 2.7%, which is a 6 basis point decrease from July 2025 (2.76%).


-


Average bankcard utilization for July 2026 was 20.4%, compared to 20.8% in July of 2025.
